title: O LET Us Our Own Works Forsake
description: O LET Us Our Own Works Forsake in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 455. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O LET us our own works for-sake, Our-selves, and all we have de-ny; Thy con-de-scend-ing coun-sel take, And come to thee pure gold to buy!

lines: O LET us our own works forsake,
Ourselves, and all we have deny;
And come to thee pure gold to buy!
O might we, through thy grace, attain
The faith thou never wilt reprove,
The faith that purges every stain,
The faith that always works by love!
O might we see, in this our day,
The things belonging to our peace
And timely meet thee in thy way
Of judgments, and our sins confess!
With filial awe revere thy rod;
And turn, with zealous haste, and run
Into the outstretched arms of God.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
